title: improve-skill-learnings: Data-Driven Skill Improvement from Captured Learnings

content.title: improve-skill-learnings: Data-Driven Skill Improvement from Captured Learnings
content.summary: Build a new skill called improve-skill-learnings that reads the unified-learnings.jsonl file, validates captured learnings against current skill/agent state, and applies cohesive fixes to the target files. The existing improve-skill gets renamed to improve-skill-benchmarks. Both form a sibling pair: benchmarks for synthetic evaluation-driven improvement, learnings for real-world failure-driven improvement. The skill handles all four improves_type values (skill, agent, process, contract), uses Haiku agents for validation and the session model for drafting changes, presents diffs for user approval, auto-commits on approval, and tracks learning status lifecycle through a new update-learning.py script.
decisions: Standalone new skill, not an extension of improve-skill
Naming pair: improve-skill-benchmarks (rename of current improve-skill) + improve-skill-learnings (new)
No args invocation. Reads unified-learnings.jsonl directly as sole input source
One skill improved per invocation. User runs again for the next skill
Filter: all entries with status == captured (both confirmed and candidate confidence levels)
Validation via Haiku agent per learning: checks staleness, correctness, and resolves target file path
Status lifecycle: captured (act on) -> applied | stale | invalid (all three skip on future runs)
Only status == captured entries enter the pipeline. stale/invalid/applied never re-investigated
Skill selection: show ranked table of skills by learning count, user picks which to improve. Null improves entries shown separately as unassigned row
Application mechanism: session-model agent reads all learnings for target skill + current file, drafts cohesive unified diff. User approves or rejects
Verification is diff review only. No automated benchmark run
Reporting: summary table (acted/stale/invalid counts) + diff + remaining captured learnings backlog count
Scope covers all four improves_type values: skill, agent, process, contract
Validation agent also resolves target file: searches skills/, agents/, resources/, scripts/ directories. If no file found, marks learning as invalid
Auto-commit after user approves the diff. Descriptive commit message referencing which learnings were applied
New update-learning.py script for status updates. Takes --id and --status args. Atomic rewrite with fcntl.flock like log-learning.py
Update learning-schema.json to add stale and invalid to allowed status enum values. Bundled with skill build
Rename of improve-skill to improve-skill-benchmarks is bundled with this work, not deferred
content.next_action: /to-tasks to break this seed into implementable task slices
implementation_decisions: Haiku validation agents run in parallel, one per learning entry
Session-model agent drafts changes, ensuring consistency regardless of which model the user is running
update-learning.py reads the full jsonl, finds entry by UUID, updates status field, rewrites atomically with file locking
learning-schema.json updated to include stale and invalid in status enum alongside captured and applied
Ranked table groups learnings by improves field, sorted by count descending. Null improves shown as unassigned row at bottom
Commit message format: improve(<target>): apply N learnings - brief description of changes
risks_and_tradeoffs: Candidate-confidence learnings may be incorrect. Haiku validation mitigates but does not eliminate risk. Diff review is the final safety gate
JSONL rewrite in update-learning.py is not append-only. File locking prevents corruption but the file must be fully rewritten on each status update
Renaming improve-skill to improve-skill-benchmarks touches many files across the repo (agent listings, settings, skill references, existing learnings data)
further_notes: 58 learnings currently captured in unified-learnings.jsonl as of 2026-09-24
Learning schema fields: type, reported_by, improves, improves_type, cause, problem, why_missed, lesson, fix, evidence, confidence, status, schema_version, id, timestamp
Existing log-learning.py handles writing. capture-learning agent handles end-of-skill capture. This new skill is the consumer side of the loop

tasks.title: Update learning schema and build update-learning.py
tasks.description: Add 'stale' and 'invalid' to the allowed status enum in learning-schema.json alongside 'captured' and 'applied'. Then build a new update-learning.py script in claude-code-shared/scripts/ that takes --id <uuid> and --status <new_status> arguments, reads unified-learnings.jsonl, finds the entry by UUID, updates its status field, and rewrites the file atomically using fcntl.flock (same locking pattern as log-learning.py). The script should validate the new status against learning-schema.json before writing. Exit 0 on success, exit 1 with stderr on validation or write failure.

tasks.title: Build improve-skill-learnings SKILL.md and register
tasks.description: Create the new skill at claude-code-shared/skills/improve-skill-learnings/SKILL.md. The skill reads unified-learnings.jsonl, filters to status == captured entries, groups by improves field, shows a ranked table sorted by count with null-improves shown as unassigned, and lets the user pick a target. For the selected target, it spawns Haiku validation agents (one per learning) to check staleness, correctness, and resolve the target file path (searching skills/, agents/, resources/, scripts/). Invalid or stale learnings get marked via update-learning.py. Surviving learnings are passed to a session-model agent that reads all of them plus the current target file and drafts a cohesive unified diff. The diff is presented for user approval. On approval, changes are applied and auto-committed with a descriptive message. A summary report shows acted/stale/invalid counts plus remaining backlog. The skill covers all four improves_type values (skill, agent, process, contract). Include the standard learning-capture block at the end. Register the skill in settings.json and agent type listings.
